status: All five stages implemented and verified; completion plan Phases 0-8 delivered (audit, database ORM integrations, auth, sessions, cache, realtime, jobs, storage, mail) — 871 runtime tests / 160 security tests / 16 type-test projects; Stage 5 CLI built last
note: Core and SvelteKit are preserved. All five stages are implemented and verified: real SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL database adapters, migrations, connection pooling, Argon2id, Redis cache/session, Stage 4 process-local adapters, and the Stage 5 sveltex CLI (built last) all ship with integration or runtime tests. 871 runtime tests, 160 security tests and 16 type-test projects pass (0 failures, 0 skipped) with live PostgreSQL 16, MySQL 8.0, Redis 7 and MinIO services. CI provisions those services. Generated apps never depend on the CLI at runtime; optional ORM integrations (Drizzle/Kysely behind optional peers) and BYO ORM adapters ship with real PostgreSQL tests, real WebSocket/SSE gateways now ship in @sveltex/realtime (single-process fan-out), while built-in Prisma/MikroORM/TypeORM adapters remain BYO-only; the S3-compatible storage adapter (Phase 7) and real SMTP/HTTP mail adapters (Phase 8) now ship (official AWS SDK v3 / nodemailer, verified against live MinIO and real SMTP/HTTP servers); no fake provider is advertised. Phase 2 extended @sveltex/auth with a concrete FixedWindowLimiter, TokenManager (single-use/expiring/purpose-scoped), PasswordResetService, EmailVerificationService and deny-by-default RBAC; OAuth2/OIDC and MFA remain explicitly out of scope. Phase 3 extended @sveltex/session with __Host- secure cookie defaults + SessionCookieTransport, double-submit CSRF (optional HMAC session binding), a persistent DatabaseSessionStore tested against real SQLite/PostgreSQL/MySQL, first-class per-user revocation (memory/Redis/SQL), and an AuthSessionPort bridge verified with a real AuthService + Argon2Hasher. SvelteKit handle-hook wiring remains Phase 10. Phase 4 extended @sveltex/cache with a typed error hierarchy, a strict versioned serialization envelope, escaped namespaces, key/prefix/predicate/tag invalidation (Redis INCR generations), an observable graceful-fallback circuit breaker, process-local single-flight with TTL jitter, and six new subpath exports; a distributed lock and additional backends are not claimed. Phase 5 extended @sveltex/realtime with a strict versioned wire protocol (direction enforcement, byte bounds, strict envelopes, no silent JSON coercion), real ws-based WebSocket and node:http/fetch SSE gateways and client transports, deny-by-default gateway authentication, heartbeats, capped reconnect with re-subscribe/queue drain, bounded backpressure, four new subpath exports and three typed errors; cross-instance brokers, persistence, TLS termination and distributed locks are not claimed. Phase 6 extended @sveltex/jobs with real Redis (ioredis + Lua) and SQL (SQLite/PostgreSQL) durable queues, a strict versioned envelope, a registry and a scheduler; Phase 7 extended @sveltex/storage with a real S3-compatible driver (AWS SDK v3), SigV4 presigned GET/PUT URLs with bounded TTL, S3 user-metadata integrity and 9 real MinIO integration tests (never skipped); Phase 8 extended @sveltex/mail with attachments, a real RFC 5322/2045 MIME serializer, SmtpTransport (nodemailer, AUTH/STARTTLS/implicit TLS), HttpTransport (strict v1 JSON envelope, SSRF guard, no redirects), auth-workflow senders, 10 new security findings (SEC-072 - SEC-081) and 24 real SMTP/HTTP/auth integration tests (never skipped). The CLI registry now advertises only real in-package adapter subpaths, verified by a consistency test. The Existing Package Completion Plan is the active roadmap (Phases 0-8 delivered; Phases 9-12 remain).
